Lupus is an autoimmune disorder characterized by chronic inflammation and damage to various organs. The primary treatment involves managing symptoms and preventing flare-ups. Common treatments include non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), corticosteroids, immunosuppressants, and biologics. Lifestyle modifications, such as stress reduction, regular exercise, and a healthy diet, also play significant roles in managing the condition.
